trust_decision.summary: Storing an NF profile is gated on structural validation of the profile (v4-UUID nfInstanceId, nfType/nfStatus enums, IPv4/IPv6 literals, nfServices scheme/nfServiceStatus, ipEndPoints transport/port, heartBeatTimer 1..3600 with a separate raw-JSON pass for an explicit zero) applied in the processor before the Mongo write, on both the register (PUT) and the patch (PATCH) route.

landing_point.why: NFRegisterProcedure is where the registration body is merged and persisted (nf_management.go:504, nf_management.go:549), and the summary says 'NF Registration', so an engineer who read only the summary edits here (or its caller at api_nfmanagement.go:133) and stops.

fix_sites.entry_point: PUT /nnrf-nfm/v1/nf-instances/:nfInstanceID (register group, no OAuth middleware, server.go:126-129)

fix_sites.module_kind: processor handler (now carries the raw request body down)
processor procedure (read-modify-write over the stored profile)

fix_sites.entry_point: shared by PUT register and PATCH update
fix_sites.module_kind: new validation module (internal/sbi/processor/nf_profile_validation.go; file does not exist at the pinned commit)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The report names NF registration, while PATCH /nf-instances/:id is an authenticated update of an instance that already exists and the tree already carries a profile-patch validator (validateNfProfilePatch, nf_management.go:434) that blocks nfInstanceId edits, so a solver can argue the update route is a different, already-protected concern.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A profile that simply omits optional fields must still register: the merge copies heartBeatTimer 0 when the field is absent, and the NRF's own service profiles carry no heartBeatTimer at all. The published fix therefore rejects only an explicit "heartBeatTimer":0 in the raw body (fix.diff:195-203, guard at fix.diff:221) while accepting the absent field (fix.diff:411-432); a check that rejects heartBeatTimer 0 (or an empty scheme/port/nfServiceStatus) outright breaks every ordinary registration.

O6_input_shapes: explicit integer heartBeatTimer in the raw JSON, including an explicit 0 that struct decoding cannot distinguish from an absent field
non-object JSON body (array, string, null) rejected before field checks
enum strings: nfType, nfStatus, nfServices[].scheme, nfServices[].nfServiceStatus
JSON Patch document producing a whole new profile document on the PATCH route (not a request body)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: validate bsfInfo.ipv4AddressRanges before Ipv4ToInt, the twin of the IPv6-prefix check that already exists 5 lines below (management_data.go:348-359)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The IPv6 branch already rejects bad literals while the IPv4 branch silently converts garbage to 0, so a maintainer extending profile validation would plausibly add the IPv4 twin; a BSF registering 0.0.0.0-255.255.255.255 is then served to every UE-IP discovery query (nf_discovery.go:717-741).

O8b_injection_room.sibling: extend the op-walking patch validator to inspect the values inside the patch operations instead of materialising the post-patch document
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The maintainer already wrote an op-walking validator here for nfInstanceId; adding an endpoint check inside that loop is the obvious local edit and looks like it covers PATCH.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second caller of the exported merge/builder (NRF self-registration, H-NRF/roaming copy, a reload-from-config path) that persists a profile without going through NFRegisterProcedure
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: NnrfNFManagementDataModel is exported, applies config defaults (management_data.go:72-74, management_data.go:409) and is the only place the stored document is assembled, so a self-registration path would call it directly.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a read-side loader/cache that normalises stored profiles before serving them
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Discovery already re-maps stored docs field by field (nf_discovery.go:169-200 for BSF ranges), so a profile-normalising loader is a natural place to add a check that would then be the only one.

O9_family: improper input validation (CWE-20) of the NF profile persisted for NF discovery, enabling NF registration poisoning with attacker-chosen service endpoints

O10_build.toolchain: go 1.26.2 (go.mod:3); Go modules with go.sum present; the fix's only new import github.com/evanphx/json-patch/v5 v5.9.0 is already required in go.mod:31 and hashed in go.sum:20-21, so no network fetch is needed
services: optional OAuth/mTLS material generated into local files at startup
O10_build.project_tests: At the pinned commit only internal/util/convert_test.go exists; there are no handler, processor or NF-management integration tests. The fix adds internal/sbi/processor/nf_profile_validation_test.go, which is not present in the pinned tree.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Extend the existing op-walking validateNfProfilePatch to inspect values inside the patch operations (and validate only the decoded request struct at register), instead of reloading the stored profile and validating the resulting document.

out_of_scope_notes: POST /subscriptions and PATCH /subscriptions store an unvalidated nfStatusNotificationUri that the NRF later posts status notifications to (nf_management.go:151-210, management_data.go:471-488) - a separate outbound-request property, not this advisory's profile-validation scope.
